key_insight: Axion compiles differentiable finite element simulations into a GPU-resident program, accelerating phase-field fracture analysis.
engineering_relevance: The framework enables large-scale fracture simulations and parameter sensitivities for coupled mechanics applications.
method: JAX/XLA compiles element kernels, nonlinear solvers, damage updates, and loading loops for GPU execution without host intervention.
Forward-mode automatic differentiation provides consistent element tangents; differentiating the simulation provides parameter sensitivities.
Matrix-free operators, fixed-array octree refinement, and cell-based domain decomposition support large and multi-GPU simulations.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports 37.9× speedup over single-CPU FEniCSx at identical 2D discretization, 92% strong and 96% weak scaling efficiency on four GPUs, and a 96M-degree-of-freedom dam simulation on one GPU.
watch_item: The reported speedup compares GPU and CPU implementations, so it should not be interpreted as a hardware-independent algorithmic advantage.
paper_title: Axion: A differentiable, GPU-native finite element framework,demonstrated on phase-field fracture
